title: Service manifest, v1
description: What a service offers and asks for, committed at its repository's root as brunna-service.yaml. Everything in it is relative to the repository and true on every machine: no path of a machine, no port, no key, no list of who uses it. The manifest asks; the person who installs the service grants. Rules a schema can't say (paths relative with no .., names unique, reserved environment names) are checked beside it.

name.description: the service's name: lowercase letters, digits and -, 2 to 48 characters; its folder and its party id are made from it

what.description: one line: what it does, shown when it is installed and to the agents that use it

interface.description: the major version of the service's own interface (its MCP tools and CLI): raised when a change breaks callers; a consumer pins it

setup.description: commands run in the service's folder, in order, after it is installed or updated (installing its dependencies from lockfiles)

run.description: the command that runs the CLI; its arguments follow; --help lists its commands
the command that starts its MCP server on stdio; the tool list is the interface

models.description: the model calls it makes through the platform, by name: the platform picks the model for the tier

secrets.description: credentials the person installing it provides, given to it as environment variables; values are never here

name.description: the environment variable it is read from

how.description: how to get one (a page to make a key on)

optional.description: true: the service starts without it (and says what it can't do)

network.description: the hosts it reaches, shown to the person installing it

data.description: what it keeps, relative to its state folder: backed up unless backup is false

why.description: with backup: false, why it can be made or downloaded again

principal.description: true: it asks to put questions and tasks to the person it serves (Principal Handoff)
